s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest and back pain with electrocardiogram changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers, suggesting an acute cardiac syndrome
salient_findings: Persistent chest and back pain
Diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR on electrocardiogram
Elevated cardiac troponin I level of 620 pg/mL
Diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography
Cystic mass above the left atrium on contrast-enhanced CT scan
key_facts: 63-year-old woman
History of hypertension
Chest discomfort and dyspnea on exertion for two months
Sinus rhythm with occasional premature ventricular complexes on electrocardiogram
Elevated cardiac troponin I level of 620 pg/mL
Diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography
Cystic mass above the left atrium on contrast-enhanced CT scan
Mass had heterogeneous attenuation (15–56 Hounsfield units) on noncontrast images
Mass exhibited slight contrast enhancement
Transient cardiogenic shock that responded to noradrenaline support

s4.champion: Thrombosed left sinus of Valsalva aneurysm

raw.champion: Thrombosed left sinus of Valsalva aneurysm
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest and back pain, elevated cardiac troponin I level, and diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle, along with the imaging findings of a cystic mass above the left atrium with heterogeneous attenuation and slight contrast enhancement, is most consistent with a thrombosed left sinus of Valsalva aneurysm. The transient cardiogenic shock also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Aortic dissection
rejected.why: There is no mention of aortic wall abnormalities or classic dissection findings on imaging.

rejected.label: Cardiac tamponade
rejected.why: Although the patient had a cystic mass, there is no evidence of significant pericardial effusion or tamponade physiology.

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: The electrocardiogram showed diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR, but the presence of a cystic mass and the patient's overall presentation are not typical for acute coronary syndrome.

rejected.label: Bronchogenic cyst
rejected.why: While the mass is cystic, its location above the left atrium and the patient's acute presentation are not characteristic of a bronchogenic cyst.
